title: Philly's Heist: Alan Turns Stefon Diggs Into Javonte Williams and More Than Doubles His Title Odds
dek: Randy finally opened for business, and Alan walked away with the better running back, the better numbers, and a 12-point jump in the computer's eyes.
body: The details are simple. Before week 4, Randy's The fumblers sent running back Javonte Williams to Alan's Team Pillbert for wide receiver Stefon Diggs, one starter for another, no throw-ins. Both players spent all three weeks on a roster, so this was no waiver-wire flyer swap. On the scoreboard, Williams brought 45.5 points with him and Diggs brought 38. That's about 15.2 per week against roughly 12.7, and Randy took the smaller half.

The computer did not need long to deliberate. Team Pillbert's title odds jumped from 9% to 21%, more than doubling on a single transaction, and the same number the commissioner earned last week by going 3-0. The fumblers slid from 16% to 14%. Randy is still 3-0, and a two-point dip isn't a disaster. But when one side of a trade gains 12 points and the other loses 2, the algorithm has already picked a winner.

For Alan, the logic writes itself. Team Pillbert already had Jahmyr Gibbs posting monster weeks, and De'Von Achane's 1.7-point dud last week showed how quickly a backfield can turn on you. Williams gives Philliberto a steady second option in a lineup that just hung 117.88 on Jordan, and he got him without giving up anyone from that Gibbs-and-Brock Purdy core. It's a clean, cold piece of roster work, and Alan will happily tell you so.

Randy's case requires more imagination, so let's give him the benefit of the doubt. Maybe he looked at a receiver room that already features Amon-Ra St. Brown and decided one more reliable target was worth more than raw backfield points. Maybe he figures Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor have the running game covered, even after Taylor's 8.2 last week. Maybe he expects Diggs to outscore his first three weeks. The man has been the league's toughest negotiator for three seasons, so it's a little stunning that his first big deal grades out as a loss on paper.

The real verdict comes on Sunday. Alan debuts his new running back against Ramon's No Banner only HULK in the week's marquee game, which means Williams gets the toughest possible audition. Randy gets Diggs into the lineup against a Kaushal team desperate to avoid 0-4. Twelve points of title odds is a nice headline, but neither of these guys collects anything until the games are played.

social.author: Waiver Wire Wendy
social.text: Javonte Williams: 45.5 points. Stefon Diggs: 38. Title odds: Alan +12, Randy -2. I've seen fairer trades on a middle school lunch table.

social.author: Team Pillbert Fan Club (Reluctant Chapter)
social.text: 21% title odds. We didn't ask for this. We don't know how to feel. We're celebrating anyway, but quietly, out of shame.

social.author: The fumblers Faithful
social.text: Everyone grading this trade off three weeks of numbers is going to look real silly when Diggs goes off against Habibsters. Still 3-0. Still Randy's world.

social.author: BFL Insider Desk
social.text: Sources: The algorithm took less than a second to process this trade and more than doubled Philly's odds. Randy has reportedly requested a recount.

social.author: Fantasy Hot Take Hank
social.text: Javonte's first start for Team Pillbert comes against HULK. Welcome to the team, here's the final boss. Good luck, buddy.
